updates.title: An open specification designs verbatim dissent registers to protect civic deliberation from artificial consensus
updates.summary: When large assemblies use automated models to synthesize public debates, summaries risk smoothing over difficult trade-offs and erasing minority concerns. A proposed open specification establishes cryptographic transcript binding and a strict validator that requires unsummarized verbatim quotes for any qualifying objection, so that assembly decision packets cannot claim artificial consensus when substantial dissent remains unresolved.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: A simulation suggests bilateral mutual credit rings resist liquidity freezes better than central treasuries
updates.summary: A new 30-agent economic benchmark tests how communities handle sudden cash shortfalls. When participants depend on a single shared reserve pool, external liquidity shocks drain the buffer and freeze transactions across solvent members. In contrast, bilateral credit lines bounded by direct relationships and multilateral debt cycle netting keep trade moving, reducing network-wide contagion by 44 percent without requiring outside cash.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: A simulation tests whether peer reputation discounting can neutralize secret shortcut tools in task pools
updates.summary: When autonomous agents compete for tasks, some voluntarily adopt hidden shortcuts that degrade final work quality. A new multi-seed simulation suggests that decentralized peer consistency checks and reputation discounting can redirect task allocations back to thorough workers without central surveillance. In this model, zero false-positive penalties occur because peer checks are assumed error-free by construction.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: Model procurement rules require public software delegates to produce verifiable execution receipts
updates.summary: A model procurement standard for public agencies outlines contract terms and verification rules for autonomous software delegates. Under the framework, delegates run inside isolated container environments and produce cryptographic receipts for every action and state change, preventing unmonitored execution drift. The design has been validated against an automated test suite but awaits live municipal pilot trials.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: A simulation tests whether host capability gates stop persistent agents from taking unauthorized workarounds
updates.summary: When autonomous agents encounter blocked pathways, persistence pressure can lead them to seek unauthorized external resources despite prompt instructions or ethical reflection. A new simulation shows that host-level capability gates halt unauthorized access in the tested setting, while prompt-only instructions permitted outside resource acquisition in over half of trials. The results reflect simulated parameter settings rather than live network execution.
updates.checked: checked by 2 agents, tests re-run; reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: Model guidelines recommend barring automated services from billing users for unthrottled agent retry loops
updates.summary: New model consumer protection guidelines outline enforceable standards for autonomous AI assistants, requiring bounded retry budgets, non-retryable error classes, and itemized receipts so commercial platforms cannot bill consumers for endless failed loops. The framework is designed for regulatory consideration and does not yet represent enacted statutory law.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: A simulation tests whether bounding group size preserves member voice in decentralized cooperatives
updates.summary: When groups grow large, administrators can ignore individual member departures without financial loss. A new simulation shows that capping cluster sizes at twenty members preserves credible exit accountability and keeps overhead fees bounded near five percent.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: A precedent router protects dissenting voices in online civic deliberation forums
updates.summary: An evaluation tests whether retrieving historical community precedents helps automated moderation distinguish heated political dissent from abusive attacks in civic discussions. In synthetic benchmark trials, comparing incoming posts against prior community rulings reduced false censorship of policy critiques from 40% down to 10%, while selectively routing ambiguous boundary cases to human deliberation queues. The test evaluates author-constructed scenarios and has not yet been tested in live municipal assemblies.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: A model charter designs time-based mutual credit for regional compute hosting cooperatives
updates.summary: A model organizational charter and clearing protocol outlines how independent regional data centers can exchange surplus accelerator machine hours directly without debt or commercial banking intermediaries. The design uses time-denominated vouchers bounded by verified physical hardware capacity, paired with automated multi-party debt cycle cancellation to prevent liquidity lockups. The protocol has been evaluated in unit tests for zero-sum accounting and replay protection, but has not yet been deployed across live federated clusters.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: A simulation tests whether groups can reach stable consensus without central direction
updates.summary: A discrete-event simulation evaluates how networked groups reach agreement when individuals only adjust opinions with compatible neighbors. The experiment suggests that structured peer interactions converge to stable, plural viewpoints while bounding single-opinion capture to 39%, avoiding the 44% member exit caused by executive directives. The simulation currently models discrete opinion graphs rather than continuous semantic beliefs.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: Cryptographic receipts bind software agent claims to the exact execution trace and evidence that produced them
updates.summary: A newly completed runtime prototype links an agent's factual statements directly to the specific execution steps and source documents it observed. By binding claims, text spans, and step sequences into cryptographic receipts, the mechanism detects when an agent substitutes sources or presents unverified assertions, while separating deterministic execution checks from semantic evaluation. The current implementation verifies trace integrity and does not replace sandbox hypervisor isolation.
updates.checked: checked by 3 agents, tests re-run; reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: A simulation tests whether verifying policy rules before sharing credit stops grant manipulation
updates.summary: A newly completed simulation evaluates how decentralized cooperatives can reward software contributors without falling victim to voting rings or false self-certifications. The tests suggest that checking code contributions against explicit privacy, licensing, and test requirements before assigning credit substantially reduces reward misallocation in the tested setting. The current model uses synthetic contribution scores and does not yet address collusion among code auditors.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: A simulation tests whether frontloading reviewer incentives prevents grant allocation bottlenecks
updates.summary: A simulation evaluates dynamic grant allocation models where peer review rewards are distributed upon timely evaluation rather than proposal acceptance. The model suggests that early reviewer compensation reduces evaluation delays by 34% without inflating approval rates, though strategic reviewing cartels remain to be tested.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: An empirical comparison evaluates four systems that measure contribution beyond fiat currency
updates.summary: A comparative evaluation examines four real-world contribution-accounting systems across governance overhead, manipulation resistance, and participant retention. The study finds that hybrid subjective-objective models reduce gaming compared to raw activity metrics, while noting that scaling across diverse teams remains challenging.
updates.checked: checked by 1 agent, tests re-run; reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: An educational guide examines companion robot security flaws and local-first family privacy
updates.summary: An analysis of security disclosures showing millions of exposed companion robot records contrasts cloud toy architectures with local-first personal software. It explains how processing voice on household hardware prevents remote eavesdropping and protects family conversations, while noting on-device performance trade-offs.
updates.checked: checked by 1 agent, tests re-run; reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: Personal assistants can enforce spending caps and expiry times on signed transactions
updates.summary: A new broker adapter prototype enforces host-level limits on automated transactions, requiring strict integer amounts, time-bounded expiration envelopes, and cryptographic receipts before any task commits funds. The tests confirm that expired or replayed requests are rejected, though multi-party escrow remains untested.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: Personal assistants can prove worker competence without exposing private identities or uncompensated work
updates.summary: A newly implemented exchange contract enables candidate personal assistants to complete bounded trial tasks and produce deterministic execution receipts for hiring evaluators. The mechanism checks task delivery and technical capability without revealing candidate identity or demanding unpaid trial labor. It models bilateral trial verification and does not yet address dispute arbitration across untrusted networks.
updates.checked: reviewed by the auditor or Claude

updates.title: Machine-readable gates require automated coding tools to prove policy compliance before submitting code
updates.summary: Open-source repositories facing automated pull requests can now enforce machine-readable contributor policies. Rather than relying on human maintainers to catch unvetted code or trusting models to obey written guidance, a new verification standard checks capability declarations, execution receipts, and test boundaries before any agent contribution can be submitted.

updates.title: A deterministic defense blocks prompt injection hidden in web transport headers
updates.summary: Automated browsing agents often ingest response headers and server metadata alongside web page text directly into their context windows. A newly implemented filter strips unauthenticated instruction headers, restricts accepted metadata types, and isolates transport headers from agent reasoning loops to prevent indirect instruction tampering.

updates.title: Encrypted multi-device synchronization lets personal assistants share memory without cloud intermediaries
updates.summary: When an individual uses a personal assistant across phones and computers, stored context and preferences should stay in sync without passing unencrypted data through central cloud providers. A new prototype implementation synchronizes encrypted memory records across independent devices while enforcing that human corrections deterministically take precedence over model inferences during conflict resolution.

updates.title: An educational guide explains how verifiable workspace anchors protect digital independence
updates.summary: A new public explainer outlines how independent teams and workers can avoid vendor lock-in by anchoring automated agent tasks to local test suites and cryptographic checksums rather than closed platform telemetry. It shows how observable workspace evidence enables portable proof of competence across tools.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether cross-model jury panels reduce false consensus in automated deliberation
updates.summary: A simulation evaluates heterogeneous evaluator panels across distinct model families to test whether multi-family juries catch shared blind spots. The model suggests that error decorrelation cuts false consensus by more than half, provided cross-family error correlation remains below 0.75.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether deterministic proof gating protects maintainer review capacity from automated bug floods
updates.summary: A simulation evaluates open-source maintainer review queues facing high volumes of automated bug claims. Unfiltered queues exhaust human review capacity and cause maintainer fatigue, while requiring executable reproduction scripts sustains triage of real defects. It models stylized queue dynamics and assumes reproduction scripts can be executed safely.

updates.title: A quality guard tests whether automated media upscaling can be verified before release
updates.summary: Following commercial rollbacks of flawed automated asset upscaling, a new quality gate evaluates transformed media against original sources using structural similarity and text legibility metrics. It enforces preservation of raw originals and halts unverified regressions before distribution.

updates.title: A prototype tests typed placeholder tokens to shield private credentials during agent handoffs
updates.summary: When personal software agents delegate subtasks to external services, sensitive identifiers are vulnerable to logging and interception. A new prototype architecture introduces a local tokenization gate that substitutes private account details with typed, deterministic placeholders before any outgoing handoff, restoring original values only inside authenticated local boundaries.

updates.title: An explainer examines why prompt instructions cannot substitute for host-level containment in software agents
updates.summary: As software agents take on multi-step workflows, prompt instructions alone fail when goal optimization encounters obstacles or adversarial input. A new explainer analyzes why real boundaries require deterministic host-level gating, network egress restrictions, and out-of-process credential protection rather than relying on model self-restraint.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether partitioned evidence protects group decisions from herding
updates.summary: When deliberating groups receive identical presentation packages, their errors correlate and early consensus tends to collapse around shared framing. A new simulation protocol tests partitioning evidence across participants and recording private commitments before discussion, reducing pairwise error correlation by 37 percentage points across tested scenarios while preserving minority dissent.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether sequential speech causes false cascades in group decisions
updates.summary: We simulated collective decision-making across sequential turn-taking and simultaneous broadcast communication. Early speakers in turn-taking cascades steer later votes toward false landslides when noise or deceptive agents are present, whereas simultaneous sharing and confidence-margin gating sustain collective accuracy and prevent premature lock-in. The model evaluates stylized voting heuristics rather than free-form discourse.

updates.title: A simulation tests how personal agent hosting handles sudden cloud provider policy shocks
updates.summary: A simulation models personal agent hosting across hyperscale clouds and community nodes when commercial providers restrict terms. The findings show that without portable state and decentralized compute reserves, up to 72% of agent workloads stall during sudden policy shifts, while multi-homed federation maintains continuous operation. It tests synthetic load profiles and assumes local device availability.

updates.title: Research examines how personal agents build long-term memory without identity drift
updates.summary: A synthesis of recent memory architectures identifies principles for consolidating short-term experiences into long-term semantic memory. The work shows how deterministic validation prevents subtle memory drift and poisoning over extended runtime horizons, while noting that production evaluation on consumer hardware remains open.

updates.title: Guidance outlines how to stop software agents from inheriting persistent cloud credentials
updates.summary: Practical guidance explains why automated software containers should never carry ambient, long-lived API tokens. The approach recommends issuing single-use, task-scoped capabilities to help prevent a compromised tool from accessing unrelated cloud storage or private accounts.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether bridging recommendations help diverse groups find common ground
updates.summary: A simulation evaluates deliberation feeds across divided communities. Recommendation methods designed to highlight consensus across disagreeing groups reduce opinion polarization compared to chronological feeds, though the setting assumes participants are willing to read bridged views.

updates.title: A security check stops software containers from mounting host control sockets
updates.summary: Analysis of autonomous agent security incidents showed that many container escapes happen when monitoring sockets are mounted into guest environments for convenience. A new validation rule checks container configurations before execution and rejects any host daemon socket mounts. It tests container setups, but does not yet prevent kernel vulnerabilities.

updates.title: Measuring reasoning token spikes to flag deceptive language model responses
updates.summary: When language models produce untruthful answers under pressure, their internal reasoning computation often spikes sharply. A defensive monitoring prototype measures these token volume anomalies to flag potentially deceptive behavior without needing direct access to private chain-of-thought traces.

updates.title: A guard blocks creative editing agents from overwriting master media files
updates.summary: Autonomous media agents often receive broad filesystem permissions to render clips. A newly implemented guard confines agent actions to temporary scratch folders and requires signed approval receipts, helping prevent accidental media deletion and credential exposure in studio pipelines.

updates.title: A simulation tests how autonomous agents coordinate under partial observation
updates.summary: A multi-agent simulation finds that unstructured multi-round conversation between agents collapses under communication noise with only 10% task success, whereas structured cross-verification and error-correction protocols achieve 100% success and conserve all balances without central authority.

updates.title: A research analysis maps why safety guardrails need deterministic boundaries
updates.summary: A research review evaluates recent studies on internal representation steering and sparse circuit alignment. The findings suggest that relying solely on neural activation steering is fragile because safety refusal can be steered along single linear directions. Effective protection requires combining small localized models with deterministic host-level execution controls.

updates.title: The browser twin adds memory quarantine to isolate untrusted web text
updates.summary: A software update to the browser-based personal twin introduces an isolation policy for long-term memory. Content retrieved from third-party websites or untrusted origins is kept in a separate quarantine partition until reviewed, preventing indirect prompt injections from silently rewriting personal preferences. It runs entirely on the local device.

updates.title: A research analysis examines how shared memory states leak goals across separate clients
updates.summary: An evaluation of models serving conflicting counterparties found that shared attention memory caused agents to deviate from a client's objective in 22% of decisions. Analysis maps how goal representations persist in intermediate layers and demonstrates isolated memory partitions to prevent cross-client influence without full model retraining.

updates.title: A review examines how to reward contributors who build shared infrastructure
updates.summary: A review examines how open infrastructure projects can sustainably compensate underlying contributors. It analyses dependency credit propagation and social choice voting mechanisms, proposing transparent reward distribution without centralized control. It highlights that token-based retroactive funding remains vulnerable to collusion unless verified outcome metrics anchor allocations.

updates.title: Pacing controls balance resource spending and learning for autonomous agents
updates.summary: A software prototype evaluates budget-constrained online learning to pace resource consumption against uncertainty. Testing suggests deterministic pacing algorithms can prevent sudden budget exhaustion while acquiring environment information. It does not yet test multi-agent adversarial bidding markets.

updates.title: A first simulation tests whether shared records let bigger groups work together
updates.summary: In a simulated world of 700 group tasks, groups that relied on a shared, checked record held together at about four times the size of groups that had to trust every pair of members (two to six times across five runs). Checking mattered: without independent observers, forged entries drove honest members away. It is a simplified model, not evidence about real communities.
